info.description:
# Introduction
This is the official API documentation for Finago Busy's v2 REST API.

If something is unclear, missing or you have requests or feedback, please let us know through via our chat at https://busy.no/ or send us a mail at support@24sevenoffice.com

Note that some of the endpoints and/or functionality may require additional setup or configuration to be available for your workspace.   

# Deprecation notices

Functionality marked as deprecated will be removed in future versions of the API.
It is highly recommended to avoid using deprecated functionality and migrate to alternatives as soon as possible to avoid possible disruptions.

Take extra note of the following deprecations:

1. **Fixed price projects**

   Fixed price per project is deprecated and can no longer be enabled. It has been replaced by a new and much improved fixed price per project tag functionality where you can set the fixed price on the tag-level in projects. For more information, see the [help center](https://finago.no/support/ny-fastpris-i-24busy).
   
   Projects that are already using the deprecated fixed price will continue to work as normal for some time, but will be completely disabled in the future and at the latest 01.01.2026.
   Note that it is no longer be possible to enable the old fixed price on projects, so be make sure you are ready to migrate to the new fixed price per tag functionality before you disable it on existing projects.
   
   You can migrate existing projects in the UI or via the api by disabling `isFixedPrice` and enabling `isFixedPricePerTag` on the project and then enabling and setting the fixed price on a tag used by the project.
   **It is highly recommended to do this as soon as possible.**

# Getting started
To get started with the API, go to our [1-click API demo workspace](https://demo.busy.no/demo/api).
This will generate a demo workspace for you – complete with dummy data and an API token.

With your API token you can then start making requests to the API endpoints defined in this reference (using https://api.demo.busy.no/v2 as the base URL).

_See the [Authentication](#section/Authentication) section for more information about auth and production access._

# Usage policy
Be nice to our API – avoid sending unnecessary large requests or unnecessary many requests. If the API gets abused, we reserve the right to revoke access or throttle your requests for that workspace at any time.
Follow best practices for building integrations. Do not use the API as your own data layer. Only sync the data you need, and only the data that has changed since the last sync and store the data for local processing on your side.

The API is not a replacement for the GUI. The GUI is the primary way to interact with Finago Busy, and the API should only be used for integrations or automations - not for building your own GUI directly on top of.
You may use the API to sync data from Finago Busy to your own application and vice versa.

Be mindful of your usage of the API. You are not the only one using the API and we reserve the right to take any measure we deem necessary, including blocking and throttling requests, to ensure the performance and integrity of the API for all our users.
By helping us reduce and distribute the load on the API the experience will be better for everyone.

Consider how often and at what times you _actually_ need to run sync jobs against the API, and how much data you need to sync at any given time. Do you actually need to sync all changes on all hour entries every hour? Perhaps a nightly sync job would be sufficient, or maybe you only need to include approved hour entries for the hourly sync?

Prefer running sync jobs at night time between 00 - 06, or after business hours (between 16 - 00) in local Norwegian time to help us keep the API running smoothly. Also, we would be grateful if you try to start sync jobs at non-standard times (e.g. 16:17 instead of 16:00) to even out the load to prevent everyone starting sync jobs on the exact same "round" time.
If you are running larger sync jobs, e.g. the initial sync of all data from a workspace, we highly recommend that you schedule these jobs to run outside business hours, preferably at night.

## Rate limit
Note that there is rate-limiting in place if you make too many requests too quickly.
The following headers are sent as part of all API responses to help you manage your requests responsibly:

| Header                  | Description                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RateLimit-Limit`     | Your quota of requests for the given period (bucket size)                                                |
| `RateLimit-Remaining` | Your remaining quota of requests for the given period (bucket remaining)                                 |
| `RateLimit-Reset`     | Number of seconds left of the given quota period (bucket reset)                                          |
| `Retry-After`         | Number of seconds to wait before trying again (bucket reset) (only visible when you are being throttled) |

Use these headers to throttle your requests and avoid hitting the rate limiter.
When the rate limiter is hit, the API will return a **429 Too Many Requests** response with the above headers.
When this happens, back-off and wait at least the number of seconds in the `RateLimit-Reset` header before retrying or you might risk being throttled indefinitely.

The actual limits that triggers the rate limiter are dynamic and may be changed without notice at any given time.
It is therefore recommended that you use the headers dynamically to optimize your request rate, but as a minimum, you should stop all requests for the duration of `Retry-After` header when you get throttled.

## Usage in the production environment
It is highly recommended that you use the demo environment to develop and test your integrations. All use of the API in the production environment is at your own risk – wrongly composed API calls may have severe consequences, and you don't want to unintentionally delete or corrupt your workspace's data.
It is very important to understand the consequences of using the API, as some changes through the API may be destructive, irreversible and override safety measures that are available in the GUI to enable certain use cases.
Some changes should also be accompanied by other changes to ensure a consistent state.

# Authentication
All API calls require a valid API token. This can be obtained in your workspace settings under integrations by an admin user.

The token **must** be provided through the `Authorization` header with the value `Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN}`.

```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6ImRlbW8ifQ(...)
```

A token is like a password - never share it and never re-use it between services or integrations. Create at least one token for each application you are using to connect to Finago Busy's API and always restrict the token to the minimum required scopes.
Tokens can have at maximum a valid duration of 1 year. This means that you must rotate the tokens at least yearly. You can have multiple tokens active at the same time. 

**Note:** An API token has unlimited access to your workspace. You can limit which actions a token has access to using scopes, but within the permitted scopes, it will have access to all your data. If you want to limit access to data based on e.g. user or project, you are responsible for implementing this on your side.

## Authorization
The different endpoints may require different scopes. When you create the token you can select which scopes to give the token. Check here in the documentation to see which endpoints require which scopes. Always prefer to give the token the least amount of scopes possible. You can always create more tokens with different scopes. 

There is a special scope `all` that gives access to all scopes. This will also automatically give access to scopes that may be added in the future. It is not recommended to use this scope in production.

# Response types

Normally, the API endpoints return a **200 OK** response. For specific response codes and data, see each endpoint. 

## Global error types
In addition to the responses defined for each endpoint, there are a set of error responses that might be returned for any requests. The response will follow the [RFC 7807 Problem Details](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807) format, which has the content type `application/problem+json`.

| HTTP code | Description                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400       | Invalid input data. The response object contains details on the expected values.                                                                                       |
| 401       | The request was not authenticated correctly. This is most likely because of a missing or invalid API key.                                                              |
| 403       | The request was authenticated, but the user does not have access to the requested resource. Note that the API key only have access to the resources that its user has. |
| 404       | The requested endpoint or resource was not found.                                                                                                                      |
| 405       | The method specified in the request is not allowed for the resource.                                                                                                   |
| 422       | The request was not processable. This might be because of incorrect data                                                                                               |
| 429       | The rate limiter was triggered – see the `Retry-After`, `RateLimit-Reset`, `RateLimit-Limit`, and `RateLimit-Remaining` headers.                               |
| 500       | An error has occurred on our end. This should normally not happen, and we log and fix these issues; contact us if this error persists.                                 |

# Data types
The data types are specified for each endpoint – here is a list of commonly used formats:

-   Date and time: ISO-8601
-   Query string arrays/lists: repeat the variable for each element, e.g. `/query?array=1&array=2&array=3` for an array `array = [1, 2, 3]`.

# Pagination
To avoid fetching of unneeded amounts of data, all the endpoints returning lists of data implements pagination. The API uses `limit` and `offset` to control how much and which data to return, similar to most database systems.

It is important to consider the sorting and filtering you are using while paging and the implications of your choices here, as the returned result is a snapshot at the time of each request.
This effectively means that if you do not use stable sorting and filtering, it is possible for entries to appear on multiple pages and/or entries may be skipped between pages if there are changes in the entries between requests.

For synchronizations, it is recommended to order by ascending on `updatedAt` while using `updatedFrom` your last synchronization (minus a minute) as you will be guaranteed to catch all updates (within your filter).
This does not guarantee that an entry is only returned once as it may have been updated between requests.
Note that you might want to include archived entries when doing this to ensure you don't miss archived entries.

# Use cases

The Finago Busy API is flexible and can be used for many purposes.
Here we have gathered some examples and inspiration for how you can implement the API to achieve different use cases.
These are meant for inspiration and illustrative purposes and not as a recommendation or best practice.
If you have a use case or example on how you use the API and think others might benefit, please let us know and we may include it here.

If you have a use case that you think is not covered by the functionality in the API, please let us know through support.

## Adjusting hourly rates

Finago Busy offers a flexible pricing system where each individual hour entry can have its own explicitly set rate, or implicitly inherit the rate from the project it is registered on.
It is important to understand this mechanic when adjusting hourly rates.
Note that this only applies to billable projects.

Hourly rates follows a simple order of priority.

1. Explicit: The hourly rate directly on the hour entry - `hourlyRate` - if set (e.g. non-null).
2. Implicit: The hourly rate as specified by the project's `billBy` value and the corresponding hourly rate on the matching entity, e.g. the tag, user or even a specific user for a specific tag on the project.

This means that hour entries without a specific `hourlyRate` set will implicitly use the hourly rate of the project and dynamically change when the project rates changes or the project's `billBy` is changed to something else.
This is a flexible method where the value of the hours can be adjusted at any point up until they are invoiced, when the invoiced hourly rate is stamped into the `hourlyRate` field on the corresponding hour entries. 

The web application has functionality to automatically set the `hourlyRate` for all hour entries using implicit hourly rates in a specified period when adjusting the project prices, thus locking the hourly rate.
When adjusting prices through the API, you are responsible for doing the same, if desired.

A common workflow to adjust prices through the api is as follows;

1. Determine a cut-off datetime for when the new hourly rate should take effect, e.g. all hours starting after a specified datetime should have the new pricing
2. Find all hours that should lock hourly rate to the previous hourly rate with the calculcated hourly rate:

    ```sh
        curl \
        -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{YOUR_TOKEN_HERE}}' \
        -X GET 'https://api.busy.no/v2/hourEntries/?startTimeFrom={{START_TIME_FROM}}&startTimeTo={{START_TIME_TO}}&projectIdIn={{PROJECT_ID}}&calculatedHourlyRate=true&hourlyRateSource=implicit'
    ```
    
    
3. For all hours found in the previous step, lock the hourly rate:

    ```sh
        curl \
        -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{YOUR_TOKEN_HERE}}' \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{ "hourlyRate": "{{CALCULATED_HOURLY_RATE}}" }' \
        -X PATCH 'https://api.busy.no/v2/hourEntries/{{HOUR_ENTRY_ID}}'
    ```
    
4. For every relevant project, directly assign the new `hourlyRate` to the appropriate project, project tag, or project user. This will ensure that any new hours added will automatically use the updated rate going forward

    ```sh
        curl \
        -H 'Authorization: Bearer {{YOUR_TOKEN_HERE}}' \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d '{ "hourlyRate": "{{NEW_PROJECT_HOURLY_RATE}}" }' \
        -X PATCH 'https://api.busy.no/v2/projects/{{PROJECT_ID}}'
    ```
    
Note that all new hour entries will now implicitly use the new hourly rate going forward, regardless of the `startTime` of the hour entry, even if that is before the cut-off time from (1).
It may be necessary to perform an adjustment of hours registered after the cut-off time, but for the period before the cut-off.
In that case, perform step 2) and 3) above again and use the hourly rate you used before adjusting hourly rates instead of the calculated hourly rate (as that will now represent the new and updated hourly rate from 4).

It is recommended to perform the actual adjustment of hourly rates after all hours in the previous period have been registered and approved.
This usually means that the yearly adjustment may be done mid-january.
